config.grain_rationale: Each row is one current Victorian liquor licence (Licence Number unique per row) held by a licensee at licensed premises. Entity fields describe the licensee business; address fields describe the licensed premises ONLY. The licensee's postal mailing address columns are left unmapped because they describe a different location than the premises and mixing them into the same address fields would make each record claim two different addresses.

record_id.rationale: Licence Number: 465/465 present and 465 distinct (shape 99999999); identifies the licence record, not a business identifier.

fields.rationale: Column headed 'Licensee' = holder of the licence, mostly in legal-name form (PTY LTD / LIMITED / CITY OF X). Also carries officer/contact-role strings such as 'THE SECRETARY' and c/- address forms, which are gated out to null; corporate and sole-trader licensee names are kept. Confidence 0.6 reflects the mixed column.
'Trading As' is explicitly the business/trading name, distinct from the licensee column (451 distinct of 465, 99.1% present). Placeholder strings nulled.
Street address of the licensed premises (present 94.2%). Premises address, not postal.

Suburb of the licensed premises (95.7% present). 7 records carry the placeholder '[Not applicable] -' (remote/pre-retail sellers without premises, shape '[a a] -'); after upper+trim the '[NOT APPLICABLE] -' gate nulls these so no bogus locality is emitted.
Premises postcode; 438 4-digit values plus 7 placeholder '0' values which are nulled. Postal postcodes are not used here (some are interstate, e.g. '2000').
Publisher-assigned licence number, unique per row.
13 publisher licence categories, kept in the publisher's wording.
Licence category states the licensed trade; the anzsic_vic_liquor_category table's keys are exactly this source's 13 category values.
Trading-hours condition attached to the licence (e.g. 'Trading to 1am', 'Ordinary').
Published maximum patron count for the premises; 60% present.
Local government area of the licensed premises.
Publisher's licensing region for the premises (Metro North, Gippsland, Hume ...).
Second publisher region label per site (Metro/Regional); one value per observation.
Latitude first then longitude, joined with ','; 94% present.
Licensee's postal mailing address — the subject's correspondence address, separated from the premises address by claim_scope.
Postal suburb; some carry an interstate state suffix (e.g. 'SYDNEY NSW') which is stripped.
Postal postcode of the correspondence address (includes interstate codes).

constants.rationale: Victorian liquor licence register published by Liquor Control Victoria; licensed premises are in Victoria.

config.notes:
XLSX: 4 title/branding rows precede the header (skip_rows=4); sheet 'Current_Victorian_Licences_By_L'; 465 data rows, 21 columns incl. two pairs of empty spacer columns. Sheet subtitle states 'Current Victorian Liquor Licences as of 31/08/2026' - a snapshot date, not per-record; observed_at falls back to dataset metadata. Nothing in the data changes per record over time, so address columns need no validity dates. No ABN/ACN column: Licence Number is 8-digit (ABN checksum 0%, ACN checksum 9.2% = chance) - deliberately unmapped. entity_type unmapped (no column states legal entity type). REVISION 3: adopts the reviewer's approved scope unchanged (premises address only; ALL postal columns unmapped) and adds ONLY the placeholder handling: '[Not applicable] -' in Suburb (7 rows, shape '[a a] -') is upper-cased and gated out at address.locality; the same '[NOT APPLICABLE] -' placeholder is nulled in address.full and the '0' postcodes in address.postcode so no placeholder value can be emitted.

[ext-v1] Licence role keyed on Licence Number; premises role keyed on the address triple. Approved address.* rules are moved to the premises role via base_rule_edits (role + establishment_address scope) rather than duplicated as new rules, so the premises address no longer competes with the licensee postal address; Postal* columns are emitted as the subject's correspondence_address. Licence status is left unmapped because the source states no licence status column; entity_type and legal_form are not inferred from name suffixes (ALDI FOODS PTY LIMITED etc.). Trading Hours is kept only as a licence condition in publisher wording, even where a cell repeats a category name. Industry code comes only from the reviewed anzsic_vic_liquor_category table; the 75 'Limited Licence' rows are dropped by the crosswalk rather than guessed. The 7 rows with postcode '0' lose locality/postcode under the approved regex/postcode ops - pre-existing approved behaviour, unchanged here.

holdout_issues.message: placeholder-like values emitted as data: ['NOT APPLICABLE']

fields.reason: Street Address is the licensed premises address; trimmed and placeholder-nulled. Emitted as establishment_address for the premises role. Correct.
Suburb is the premises locality; '[Not applicable] -' placeholders are nulled. Observed values (MT BULLER, BENDIGO, etc.) match the premises address, and the scope matches.
Postcode of the premises, placeholder '0' nulled. Observed values are consistent with the suburb. Postal postcodes are correctly kept separate.
Licence Number is publisher-assigned and unique per row; attaches to licence.
Licence Category kept in publisher wording, verbatim.

Crosswalk is draft (AI-prepared, unreviewed) yet produces precise ANZSIC codes that carry meaning the source category does not support: 'BYO Permit' → 4511 (Cafes and Restaurants) even for 'THEODOR HERZL SOCIAL CLUB' and a ski-club lodge, 'Producer's Licence' → 121 (Grape growing, not winemaking), 'Remote Seller's Licence' → 4310 (a wholesale division). Observed codes are internally inconsistent with the licensed business. Also licence-category → industry-code is a licence-purpose inference, not a source-stated activity at division precision. Confirm review or emit at subdivision and mark provisional.

Trading Hours is genuinely a condition, but in many rows it merely repeats the category string ('BYO Permit', 'Producer's Licence', 'Pre-retail Licence', 'Limited Licence'), so the observation is not a distinct condition value and adds noise; the licence-category value is duplicated onto the condition concept.
Patron Capacity → establishment.capacity, integer parsed. 500/257/100/24 plausible; blanks dropped.
Council is the LGA of the premises; full council name kept with 'COUNCIL' suffix, an acceptable publisher-wording value.
'Region' (Hume, Loddon Mallee, Metro South ...) is the publisher's licensing region for the site. One value per observation.
Metro/Regional is the second publisher region label; emitted separately as required by multi-valued handling.
Latitude then Longitude joined with ',' matches the 'lat,lon' definition; values inside Australia and consistent with the premises locality.
Postal Address is the licensee's mailing/correspondence address and is explicitly scoped correspondence_address, separate from the premises address. PO boxes are legitimate correspondence.
Postal Suburb with state suffix stripped ('SANDOWN VILLAGE', 'NARRE WARREN NORTH'); scoped correspondence. Character class allows the observed values.

Postal Postcode scoped correspondence; values consistent with postal suburb and can be interstate as documented. Note: premises for 'Pre-retail Licence' 33781710 was null but 'Metro/Regional' region was still emitted for the premises role — see summary.

critic.summary: Changed/new rules are mostly sound: premises address/locality/postcode/LGA/region/geo and capacity are correctly scoped to the establishment, licence number and category attach to the licence, and the postal address is deliberately and correctly separated as correspondence. The substantive doubt is rule 5: an unreviewed AI-drafted crosswalk converts licence category into specific ANZSIC 2006 codes whose division-level claims are not supported by the source category and are visibly inconsistent (social/ski clubs → 4511 cafe; producer → grape growing 121; remote seller → wholesale division 4310). Rule 6 generally duplicates the licence category into the condition field for several categories. A data issue worth flagging: in record 33781710 the premises address, locality, postcode, LGA and geo are all blank yet ext.establishment.region 'Regional' is still emitted for the premises role, i.e. a region claim on an establishment with no address evidence.

fields.reason: Street Address is the licensed premises' street address, correctly scoped to establishment_address on the premises entity; placeholder gating is sensible.
Suburb is the premises locality. The negative-lookahead gate correctly nulls '[NOT APPLICABLE] -' after upper/trim while passing real suburbs (MT BULLER, NAGAMBIE) through unchanged.
Premises postcode, placeholder '0' nulled, postcode normalisation applied; scoped to establishment_address.
Licence Number is the publisher-assigned licence identifier, unique per row, attached to the licence entity.
Licence Category kept in publisher wording and attached to the licence, not the entity.
Patron Capacity is the published maximum patron count for the premises; blanks/placeholder text dropped and parsed to integer (500, 257, 100, 24 all correct).
Council is the LGA of the licensed premises; 'NOT APPLICABLE' treated as placeholder rather than an LGA.
Region is a publisher licensing region for the site; one value per observation, consistent with the multi-valued region concept.

Metro/Regional is a second, distinct publisher region label; emitted as its own single-valued observation rather than overwriting the Region value. Note: for the pre-retail record with no premises address this yields a region on a premises entity that has no address, but the rule itself is sound.
Latitude then longitude joined with ',' gives correct 'lat,lon' ordering inside Australia; blanks produce no observation.

Postal Address is the licensee's mailing address, correctly separated from the premises address by claim_scope=correspondence_address and attached to the subject (licensee) rather than the premises. This supersedes the dataset's earlier 'left unmapped' note, but the claim_scope split resolves the two-addresses-in-one-field problem that note warned about.

Postal Suburb mapped to locality with the interstate state suffix stripped; the non-greedy capture returns the full suburb (SANDOWN VILLAGE, NARRE WARREN NORTH, SOUTH YARRA) and would reduce 'SYDNEY NSW' to SYDNEY. Scoped to correspondence_address on the subject.
Postal Postcode is the correspondence address postcode (interstate codes included) and is correctly kept separate from the premises postcode via claim_scope.

missed.reason: No licence-condition target exists in the supplied ontology, and the column largely duplicates the licence category, so leaving it unmapped is defensible; flagged only for completeness.

critic.summary: All 13 rules are sound. Premises/licence fields are attached to the right entities and roles, the premises address is consistently scoped establishment_address, and the newly added postal columns are correctly separated as the licensee's correspondence_address on the subject entity rather than being merged with the premises address. Geo ordering, capacity parsing, placeholder gating and the suburb state-suffix strip all behave correctly on the rare held-out values. Only caveat: the pre-retail record with empty premises address still emits a region on a premises entity whose key fields are all blank, and the dataset's grain note about leaving postal columns unmapped is now stale given the claim_scope split.
